title: Introduce cost-sentry sampler and quant-profile bridge for tenant warmup
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a tenant warmup sampler (cost-sentry) that generates lightweight sample traces and a quant-profile bridge that converts sampler-derived metrics into safe quantization presets. Includes telemetry, a small CLI to export/import profiles, and a gradual rollout plan with canary and soft-fallback to full-precision models.
description: Motivation: tenant onboarding and bursty traffic patterns were producing unpredictable token costs for smaller customers; manual tuning of batch/cache defaults and quant profiles is slow and error-prone. This PR introduces a lightweight sampler (cost-sentry) that collects representative traces at low QPS, scores unit economics, and produces candidate quantization profiles plus batch/cache recommendations via a quant-profile bridge. Summary of changes: 1) new sampler service under runtime/sampler that emits compact workload signatures and token-latency histograms; 2) quant-profile bridge that maps sampler signals to a ranked set of quant presets with safety thresholds (per-tenant); 3) a CLI tool (bin/rw-econ) to export/import candidate profiles and run simulated cost projections; 4) metric + tracing hooks for per-tenant econ-score, sample-coverage, and fallback-triggers; 5) rollout and migration: sampler disabled by default, opt-in via tenant config; staged rollout with 5% canary, 25% limited, then global with automatic rollback on regen-rate or quality regressions. Why this approach: automating warmup and profile generation reduces manual ops, shortens time-to-savings, and provides a safety-first path to quant adoption. Backwards compatibility: sampler output is stored as telemetry only until profile import is approved; runtime respects existing model pins and will only apply quant profiles when tenant config allows it. Testing: unit tests for sampler sketching and bridge heuristics, integration tests for CLI projections, e2e canary in perf-canary harness with synthetic workloads. Rollout plan: canary on dedicated infra for a select tenant cohort, monitor econ-score, output-quality tests (prompt suites), and latency SLOs for 48h before broader rollout. Related work: follows from ENG-1987 (tenant warmup requirements) and ENG-2022 (quant-safety thresholds). Checklist: - [x] sampler service implementation - [x] quant-profile bridge logic - [x] CLI for export/import and local simulation - [x] telemetry and dashboards - [x] unit/integration tests - [x] canary rollout configuration and feature flag
commits: 1) Implement cost-sentry sampler core loop and lightweight sketching (runtime/sampler)
2) Quant-profile bridge: heuristics + safety gates + profile serializer (runtime/quant-bridge)
3) CLI: rw-econ export/import and simulate commands (bin/rw-econ)
5) Tests and perf-canary harness config (tests/, perf-canary/)
review_thread: Alejandro Ruiz: Could we avoid adding another process by folding the sampler into the existing prefill agent? Concern: cross-contamination of resource accounting.

Maya Chen (author): I considered folding into prefill but kept it separate to allow different lifecycle and scheduling. Sampler is extremely low CPU (stateless sketches) and runs on a separate thin worker; we'll add resource caps and a scheduler group to avoid interference.
Priya Nair: The safety thresholds look conservative; do we have a mechanism to quantify false positives where quality drops but econ-score still improves?

Maya Chen: Bridge emits a 'projected-quality-delta' and we run existing eval prompt sets as a gating check in the CLI; also feature flag prevents auto-apply unless tenant opted in. We'll add a regression-alert rule in the post-merge follow-up.
Samir Patel: CI showed one flaky test on quant heuristics that passed after rebase; ensure tests are stable before wide rollout.
Maya Chen: Flaky test was due to non-deterministic RNG in a mock; fixed by seeding the mock RNG and added a determinism assertion in the test.
merge_summary: Merged by Alejandro Ruiz using squash-merge on 2026-03-07. Commit message summarizes sampler and bridge and references ENG-1987 ENG-2022. Post-merge: created dashboard 'econ/warmup/candidate-profiles', added a follow-up ticket ENG-2134 to add automated regression alerts and a migration script for tenant owners.
